title: ClangIdentity::capture launches `--version` and `-dumpmachine` on every call: 1,216 of the heaviest test binary's 4,803 Clang launches
why: Card W44-TEST-SUITE-WALL-TIME made `clang::command()` resolve and probe Clang once per QCORE_CLANG/PATH environment. That cut `unsupported_close_route_parity`'s Clang launches from 9,603 to 4,803 and the serial suite's run phase from 1,345 s to 506 s. Of the launches that remain, 608 `--version` and 608 `-dumpmachine` (25%) come from `ClangIdentity::capture`, which asks the same executable for its identity again on every call in one process (docs/reports/w44-test-suite-wall-time/evidence/clang-launches.json). The identity is provenance that the gateway already trusts to stay stable while in use. DISCHARGE: capture the identity once per resolution under that same premise, with tests showing that a changed QCORE_CLANG or PATH re-captures it and that a failed capture is not cached. Then count the launches again and re-time the suite.

title: `unsupported_close_route_parity` alone sets the end of the parallel test phase: 153-187 s of a 172-211 s run phase, 53.5 s when run serially
why: Under scripts/run_test_binaries.py (card W44-TEST-SUITE-WALL-TIME), the heaviest binary starts first and finishes last in all three final runs, at 187.4, 183.2 and 153.0 s. The next-longest binary finishes 36-42 s earlier. Changing --jobs between 4 and 16 moves the run phase only between 172 and 219 s. Sharing the CPUs makes the binary run about 3x slower than its serial 53.5 s. The binary's longest test is `both_routes_refuse_the_same_body_mutations`. For each of its 12 rows, the retained route rebuilds the file-backend evidence over the unmutated `backend::SOURCE` with the full Clang pipeline, and so does the moved route's prerequisite derivation (docs/reports/w44-test-suite-wall-time/evidence/per-binary.json). DISCHARGE: a measured cut of this binary's longest test that keeps every forged row's own core evaluation. One option is a shared retained-backend fixture with a stated equivalence argument. Report the new critical path.
